Proof. Let c_1 = c_LW and c_2 = c_acc. For history H = [Pop (x), Pop (x)]: c_LW(H) = {x 1} (last write wins, x is present once); c_acc(H) = {x 2} (two pops counted). Applying the other rule to these outputs gives different results depending on the order, since the outputs have different structures.

Theorem (Bind Commutativity Under Symmetric Dependencies). If Bind (a, b) and Bind (b, a) are both in H, then the dependency between a and b is symmetric: a A (H^*) b A (H^*) under the refusal closure.

Proof. By the Dependency Propagation Theorem, Refuse (a, r) ∈ H propagates to Refuse (b, ρ(r)) ∈ H^* via Bind (a, b), and Refuse (b, r') ∈ H propagates to Refuse (a, ρ(r')) ∈ H^* via Bind (b, a). Hence inadmissibility propagates in both directions, creating symmetric mutual inadmissibility.

nodes.title: Continuations and Counterfactuals
nodes.heading: section
text: Causal reasoning asks: what would have happened if we had done otherwise? In Spherepop, this is a question about alternative histories—histories that agree with the actual up to some point and then diverge.

Definition (Counterfactual History). A counterfactual history relative to H at step k is any history H' such that H' agrees with H on the first k-1 events and differs on event k: H[1:k-1] = H'[1:k-1] but H[k] ≠ H'[k].
Definition (Counterfactual Continuation Difference). The counterfactual difference between histories H_1 and H_2 is
[equation]
the symmetric difference of their future continuation sets.

Theorem (Counterfactual Distinguishability Theorem). If C (H_1) ≠ C (H_2), then H_1 and H_2 are computationally non-equivalent: there exists a future computation that is possible from one but not the other.

Proof. C (H_1) ≠ C (H_2) implies C (H_1) C (H_2) ≠. There exists c in the symmetric difference: c ∈ C (H_1) C (H_2) (or vice versa). This means c is reachable from H_1 but not from H_2. The two histories therefore differ in their computational potential.
Definition (Causal Influence). Event e_i in history H causally influences continuation c if removing e_i from H (and adjusting subsequent events consistently) changes whether c is reachable:
[equation]
Theorem (Pop Events Are Causally Primary). Every continuation c ∈ C (H) is causally influenced by at least one Pop event in H.

Proof. A continuation c consists of further events extending H. The specific form of c depends on what has been committed (the Pop events in H), since commitments remove alternatives and shape which future events are admissible. Removing all Pop events from H leaves only Refuse, Bind, and Collapse events, which preserve Ω and do not commit to specific paths. The set C (H_no-pop) is a superset of C (H), so specific continuations reachable from H are reachable only because specific Pop events have narrowed the possibility space in the right direction.

nodes.title: Causal Models and Spherepop
nodes.heading: section
text: Definition (Spherepop Causal Model). A Spherepop causal model is a dependency graph G_H together with a labeling of each node x with its Pop or Refuse status in history H. An intervention on x is a counterfactual history H' that changes the event at position k (where x first appears) from Pop (x) to Refuse (x, Intervened) or vice versa.

Theorem (Do-Calculus Correspondence). The Spherepop intervention operation corresponds to Pearl's do-operator: do(Pop (x)) sets x to committed status regardless of its upstream causes, which in Spherepop corresponds to adding Pop (x) to the history while severing the incoming dependency edges to x in G_H.

Proof. Pearl's do(X = x) removes the incoming arrows to X in the causal graph and sets X to x. In Spherepop: severing incoming dependency edges corresponds to removing Bind events (y, x) from G_H; setting X to committed corresponds to adding Pop (x). The resulting modified history H' is the Spherepop representation of the interventional distribution P(· | do(X = x)).

nodes.title: Note Morphisms
nodes.heading: section
text: Definition (Note Morphism). A note morphism from note N_1 to note N_2 is a function f : C (N_1) → C (N_2) that maps continuations preserved by N_1 to continuations preserved by N_2, such that P_A(f(c), t | N_2) ≥ P_A(c, t | N_1): the target note preserves the continuation at least as well as the source.

Theorem (Notes Form a Category). Notes with note morphisms form a category Notes: Objects: notes N (artifacts increasing reachability of some continuation). Morphisms: note morphisms f : N_1 → N_2. Composition: (g f)(c) = g(f(c)), which is a valid note morphism since reachability is preserved by composition. Identity: id_N(c) = c is the identity note morphism.

Proof. Composition: if f : N_1 → N_2 and g : N_2 → N_3 are note morphisms, then for any c ∈ C (N_1): P_A(g(f(c)), t | N_3) ≥ P_A(f(c), t | N_2) ≥ P_A(c, t | N_1). So g f is a valid note morphism. Identities and associativity are immediate.

nodes.title: Note Functors
nodes.heading: section
text: Theorem (The Continuation Functor). There is a functor C : Notes → Set sending each note to its continuation set and each morphism to the corresponding function on continuation sets.
Proof. C sends note N to C (N) ⊆ C _total and morphism f : N_1 → N_2 to f : C (N_1) → C (N_2). This preserves composition and identities by definition of note morphism.
Theorem (Note Composition Increases Reachability). The tensor product N_1 N_2 of two notes satisfies
[equation]
with strict inclusion when the notes enable joint continuations not reachable from either alone.

Proof. A combined note system has access to the continuations of each component plus any joint continuations enabled by having both. Since $C (N_1) C (N_2) C (N_1 N_2)$ by definition and joint continuations strictly add to the union, the inclusion is proper when $C _bind(N_1, N_2) $.

nodes.title: The Reachability Value of Knowledge
nodes.heading: section
text: Definition (Knowledge Value Functional). The knowledge value of a note N for agent A at time t is
[equation]
the total reachability gain.
Theorem (Knowledge Leverage Theorem). The knowledge value of a note equals the total increase in reachability it provides:
[equation]
where |C (N)_new| is the number of new continuations enabled and g is the average gain per continuation.

Proof. Decompose the sum: $V_K(N, A, t) = _c C (N) G_A(N, c, t) + _c C (N) G_A(N, c, t). Forc C (N),G_A(N, c, t) = 0$ by definition of the continuation set. For c ∈ C (N), the average gain is g. The result follows.

nodes.title: Libraries as Continuation Reservoirs
nodes.heading: section
text: Definition (Continuation Reservoir). A collection of notes N is a continuation reservoir for agent population A if it strictly increases total reachability:
[equation]
Theorem (Library Reachability Theorem). If each note N_i ∈ N has non-negative reachability leverage and at least one note has positive leverage, then N is a continuation reservoir.

Proof. Let Δ_i(c) = P_A(c, t | N_i) - P_A(c, t). Non-negative leverage means _c Δ_i(c) ≥ 0 for all i. Positive leverage for some N_j means _c Δ_j(c) > 0. Summing over all notes: _c,i Δ_i(c) > 0, which implies the total reachability increases.

Remark. Civilization is not primarily the accumulation of facts. It is the accumulation of preserved re-entry points into abandoned, deferred, repaired, and generative continuations. A library's value is not the mass of paper it contains but the volume of continuations it makes accessible.

nodes.title: Science as Civilizational Refusal
nodes.heading: section
text: Theorem (Scientific Progress as Directed Refusal). Scientific progress is a sequence of Refuse events applied to the space of possible theories: each failed experiment refuses a class of theories with reason ExperimentalRefutation.

Proof. A scientific experiment tests a prediction P derived from theory T. If the experiment fails (P is observed), the falsification principle (Popper) requires adding Refuse (T, Refuted(P)) to the scientific community's history. This monotonically shrinks the admissibility set of viable theories. Scientific progress is therefore the directed shrinkage of the theory-admissibility set, guided by experiment.

Corollary (Science Increases Admissibility Entropy Compression). As science progresses, the admissibility entropy of the theory space S_A (theories) decreases: fewer theories are admissible given the accumulated experimental record.

Remark. This formalizes the intuition that science constrains rather than merely accumulates. Each confirmed refutation reduces the set of viable theories, making the remaining theories more precisely constrained. The admissibility entropy of scientific theories in 2025 is dramatically lower than in 1600, not because we have proved more but because we have refused more.

nodes.title: Writing Systems as Compression Infrastructure
nodes.heading: section
text: Theorem (Writing Reduces Reconstruction Cost Across Time). A writing system reduces the reconstruction cost C_r(c, o) for observations o made before its invention by making the associated histories accessible across the temporal gap between creation and reading.

Proof. Without writing, an observation at time t_1 produces a fiber c^-1(o) at time t_2 > t_1 of size exponential in (t_2 - t_1) (all histories consistent with the biological memory trace are candidates). With writing, the fiber is reduced to histories consistent with the written record, which is exponentially smaller. Hence C_r(c, o) decreases by an amount proportional to the entropy reduction.

Example (The Rosetta Stone as Repair Note). The Rosetta Stone (196 BCE) is a repair note for the ancient Egyptian writing system. When Egyptian hieroglyphics became unreadable (the writing system was refused by history—practitioners died and the tradition collapsed), the Rosetta Stone provided a Bind event: it coupled the Greek text (whose continuation space was still accessible) to the Egyptian text (whose continuation space had become unreachable). The stone did not restore the original writing tradition, but it created a repair morphism from the collapsed tradition to a reconstructed one.

nodes.title: Programming Languages as Generative Notes
nodes.heading: section
text: Theorem (Programming Language as Maximum-Leverage Note). A general-purpose programming language L is a generative note with unbounded reachability leverage: Λ(L) → ∞ as the number of programs expressible in L grows.

Proof. The continuation set C (L) includes all computations expressible in L. For a Turing-complete language, |C (L)| is infinite (countably many programs). The creation cost C_create(L) is finite (the language was designed and implemented once). Therefore $(L) = _c P(c) / C_create(L)$ involves dividing a diverging numerator by a finite denominator: Λ(L) → ∞.

nodes.title: Legal Systems as Constraint Ledgers
nodes.heading: section
text: Theorem (Legal Code as Coordinated Refusal Note). A legal code is a Coordination Note that documents, for a community of agents, which actions are admitted (legal), refused (illegal), and under what conditions repair (amnesty, appeal, rehabilitation) is available.

Proof. A law L that prohibits action a is a Refuse event applied to all agents in the jurisdiction: Refuse (a, IllegalUnder(L)). A law that requires action b is a Bind event: Bind (citizenship, b), coupling the agent's status to the obligation. Enforcement is the execution of the refusal: making refusal-violations actually inadmissible (with sanctions). The legal system's history is the sequence of legislative acts (Pop events on the space of possible legal rules) and judicial decisions (Refuse events on specific behavioral patterns).

Example (Precedent as Collapse Note). A legal precedent (stare decisis) is a Collapse Note: it collapses the family of future cases similar to the precedent case into a single observable state (the holding). The precedent makes the collapse rule explicit: future courts must observe similar cases through the lens of the established holding, and may only refine or distinguish the rule (not ignore it).

nodes.title: Markets as Distributed Prospective Notes
nodes.heading: section
text: Theorem (Prices as Distributed Prospective Notes). A market price p for good x is a Prospective Note: it preserves access to the continuation of exchanging x at price p for all agents who observe the price signal.

Proof. A price p is a public Bind event: Bind (seller of x, buyer of x at p). It creates a prospective continuation—the exchange—that was not reachable before the price was established. Without the price signal, buyers and sellers must individually search for counterparties (high reconstruction cost). With the price signal, the continuation of exchange is directly accessible (low reconstruction cost). Market prices therefore reduce the reconstruction cost of economic coordination.

nodes.title: Formal Statement
nodes.heading: section
text: Throughout this monograph, histories and reachability have been treated as two aspects of the same underlying structure. This chapter makes the correspondence explicit.

Definition (Reachability Volume of a History). Let Fut(H) be the set of admissible continuations extending H (finite sequences of events that are admissible given H). The reachability volume of H is V_R(H) = |Fut(H)|.
Theorem (Pop Narrows Reachability). If H' = H ++ [Pop (x)], then V_R(H') ≤ V_R(H).
Proof. Every continuation extending H' is also a continuation extending H, since H' itself extends H. Thus Fut(H') ⊆ Fut(H) and V_R(H') ≤ V_R(H).
Theorem (Refuse Narrows Admissible Reachability). If H' = H ++ [Refuse (x,r)], then V_R(H') ≤ V_R(H).

Proof. A continuation extending H' must respect the refusal of x: any continuation requiring an unrepaired Pop of x is excluded from Fut(H'). Since all continuations extending H' are continuations extending H with an additional admissibility constraint, Fut(H') ⊆ Fut(H).

Corollary (Computation as Reachability Shaping). A Spherepop computation is not merely a path from input to output. It is a monotone transformation of a reachability volume: commitment (Pop) and refusal (Refuse) both narrow the reachability volume, while Bind and Collapse reshape its structure without necessarily shrinking it.

nodes.title: The History-Reachability Duality
nodes.heading: section
text: Theorem (History-Reachability Duality). There is a duality between the lattice of histories ordered by prefix extension and the lattice of reachability volumes ordered by subset inclusion:
[equation]

Proof. If H_1 is a prefix of H_2, then H_2 = H_1 ++ H' for some non-empty H'. By repeated application of Pop Narrows Reachability and Refuse Narrows Admissible Reachability (one application per event in H'), V_R(H_2) ≤ V_R(H_1).

Remark. The History-Reachability Duality is the formal content of the monograph's central thesis: computation is the progressive restriction of possibility. As the history grows (computation proceeds), the reachability volume shrinks. The history and the reachability volume are dual representations of the same computational trajectory.

nodes.title: The History-Reachability Correspondence Theorem
nodes.heading: section
text: Theorem (History-Reachability Correspondence). Let Φ : H → (C ) be the map sending history H to its reachability volume Fut(H). Then: Φ is an order-reversing map between the prefix lattice on H and the inclusion lattice on (C ). Φ preserves the Conservation Law: |Ω(H)| + |consumed(H)| = |Ω_0|. Φ(ε) = C _total (the empty history has maximal reachability). Φ(H_terminal) = when Ω(H_terminal) =.

Proof. (1) is the History-Reachability Duality theorem. (2) follows from the Conservation of Possibility: committed events (|consumed(H)|) plus remaining options (|Ω(H)|) equal the initial option count. (3) holds because the empty history has imposed no commitments, so all continuations are reachable. (4) holds because if Ω =, no further Pop events are possible, so no continuation can extend H by selection.

Remark. Theorem [thm:hrc] is the unification theorem promised from the beginning of this monograph. It shows that Spherepop's two primitive concepts—the history that computation produces and the reachability volume that computation consumes—are formally dual. Each determines the other. A complete history determines a terminal reachability volume. A specified reachability volume constrains the possible histories that could have produced it.

This duality is the same duality that appears throughout the monograph in other guises: state versus history, observation versus trajectory, collapse versus reconstruction, notes as anti-collapse artifacts.
All of these are the same duality, seen from different angles.
